article.story: CHARLESTON, S.C. -- — Aiden Derkack and Tristian Ford both scored 14 points and Dayton used a strong first half to turn back Utah 63-46 on Friday night in the Charleston Classic. The Flyers make 5 of 10 from 3-point range and shot 60% in the first half to open a 20-point lead and then held on despite going 1 of 11 behind the arc and shooting 30% in the second half. Grant Randall added 10 points for the Flyers (3-3), who overcame 18 turnovers. Trey Campbell had 16 points for Utah (3-2) and Taison Chatman added 11. The Utes shot 29% for the game. Landen Joseph hit a 3-pointer to give Dayton a 10-9 lead and Cody Peck's putback ended an 11-0 run for an 18-9 lead in the middle of the first half. Joseph hit a 3-pointer at the 7:25 mark to get the lead to double figures at 21-11 and had another in a closing 7-0 spurt to end the half with a 37-17. Joseph was injured with 7:44 and used crutches to return to the bench to watch the end of the game. It is the fewest points Dayton allowed in the first half since 1960. The Flyers closed the first half by making seven straight shots, then had a 1 of 13 stretch in the second half, although the struggling Utes, who lost to Eastern Washington at home on Tuesday, could get no closer than a dozen. Up next Dayton: vs. Northwestern in Charleston on Sunday.
